lines: {target}? Sound travels farther than sense.
That warning belongs at the start of every trip to Deep Dark. Walk soft and do not open every chest.
Sculk hears what pride forgets.
I'll remember Deep Dark as darkness that listens back.
You made it back from the deep dark. How close did that come to changing?
Did darkness change the route around the deep dark more than you expected?
I would want both hands free on uneven ground. Did you manage that?
A hard journey feels longer in poor weather. How much longer did the deep dark feel?
Tell me the truth about your supplies. How much water remained when you turned back?
I have crossed ugly water and still would not hurry toward the deep dark.
The first hot bowl after the deep dark must have settled more than hunger.
Did you carry one tool that turned out to matter more than all the rest?
Was rest possible once the sounds around the deep dark started?
Who shared the watch with you when the deep dark went quiet?
What was the first thing you heard after everyone stopped talking?
Which danger at the deep dark deserves a clearer warning for the next traveler?
Home must have looked different after the deep dark. What did you notice first?
Would better planning have changed the danger, or only your chances?
I was worried about the ending. I am glad you are here to tell it.
Who should hear this story before they make the same journey?
{target}? Stone teeth hang above and wait below.
Tell the next traveler about Dripstone Caves before they leave. Look up as often as you look down.
Pointed stone makes every stumble serious.
I will remember Dripstone Caves as a cave that bites from both directions.
Did caution arrive before the danger at the dripstone caves, or just after it?
What told you that you were still headed the right way at the dripstone caves?
Which part of the dripstone caves made you test every step before trusting it?
Did the weather near the dripstone caves give you any warning before it changed?
Did anyone underestimate how much water the journey would take?
Water has frightened me before. I can hear that the dripstone caves frightened you worse.
Which meal tasted best once you left the dripstone caves behind?
What would you remove from the pack before another trip to the dripstone caves?
What made a place feel safe enough to stop for the night?
Bad nights last longer alone. Who was awake with you?
What warning did the sounds around you give before you saw the danger?
Did you see any warning signs that only made sense afterward?
Did the weather follow you home from the dripstone caves?
The next traveler needs the honest version. Where should the story begin?
That memory still has weight. Take your time with it.
After all that, is there anything near the dripstone caves you still want to see?
{target}? Pretty caves still have long drops.
No one should approach Lush Caves without hearing this. Watch the vines and the holes between them.
Glow berries light paths that may not be safe.
I'll remember Lush Caves as a cave trying very hard to look harmless.
Some danger announces itself. What stayed hidden at the lush caves?
Where would you leave a marker if you had to approach the lush caves again?
Did your boots hold when wet stone in dark passages became dangerous?
What did you cover first when the weather turned near the lush caves?
Did the underground flow beside the path last as long as you needed it to?
At least a river tells you which way it is moving. Did the lush caves tell you anything?
Did worry take your appetite before the supplies ran low?
Was your pack too heavy when the ground became difficult?
Did anyone sleep well while dark corners and misleading echoes remained close?
Did anyone keep their nerve when the rest of you were tired?
Does the smell of the lush caves linger more than the rest of the memory?
Did the danger find you before you found a safe route?
Did anyone speak much on the way back, or were you all spent?
If the village wrote one warning about the lush caves, what should it say?
Did you feel safe only after the village door closed behind you?
What unfinished question could ever pull you back toward the lush caves?
